chief_complaint: swelling all over my body and frothy urine
hpi_details: 60F presents with 2 weeks of worsening swelling in her legs, hands, and face. She also notes her urine looks extremely foamy. She has a history of type 2 diabetes for 15 years.

core_concepts: Characterized by massive proteinuria (>3.5g/day), hypoalbuminemia, and severe edema.
Foamy urine is a hallmark of significant proteinuria.
common_misconceptions: Prescribing only diuretics without addressing the underlying proteinuria or adding ACEi/ARBs.
dangerous_errors: Missing the increased risk of DVT/PE in nephrotic syndrome due to loss of antithrombin III.
management_principles: 24hr urine protein or spot UPCR, lipid panel, start ACEi/ARB, diuretics, refer to nephrology.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 60F with long-standing diabetes presents with generalized edema and foamy urine.
reference_soap.objective: 3+ pitting edema to thighs, periorbital edema. BP 150/90. Urinalysis: 4+ protein, no blood.
reference_soap.assessment: Nephrotic Syndrome, likely secondary to diabetic nephropathy.
reference_soap.plan: Spot Urine Protein-to-Creatinine ratio. Start Lisinopril, Furosemide. Nephrology consult.

learning_objectives: Identify the clinical signs of nephrotic syndrome and relate it to diabetes.

teaching.one_liner: Anasarca and foamy urine in a diabetic patient, highly suggestive of nephrotic syndrome.
red_flags: Shortness of breath (pulmonary edema or PE)

must_ask.say: When did the swelling start, and where on your body have you noticed it?
Have you noticed your urine looking foamy or frothy?
How long have you had diabetes, and how well controlled has your blood sugar been?
Have you noticed rapid weight gain or any shortness of breath?
Have you had any leg swelling on one side, calf pain, or sudden chest pain?

history.answer: My whole body has become terribly swollen over the past two weeks, and I noticed my urine looks extremely bubbly and foamy.
It started with puffiness around my eyes and face, but now my hands, both legs, and thighs are heavily swollen.
It started gradually about two weeks ago and has been getting steadily worse every day.
My eyes and face are puffiest when I get up in the morning, while my legs feel much tighter and heavier by the evening.
When I press my shins, deep indentations stay there for a long time, and my socks and rings leave deep marks.
I weighed myself and found that I gained about 6 kilograms over the past two weeks, even though I have not eaten more.
No, neither leg is red or warm to the touch, and they do not hurt; both legs are swollen equally.
I get a bit winded when climbing stairs with this extra weight, but I do not feel breathless at rest.
No, I can lie down flat on a single pillow without any trouble, and I do not wake up gasping for air at night.
No, I have not had any chest pain, tightness, coughing, or pain in my chest.
Yes, whenever I urinate, the bowl fills with thick foam that does not wash away when flushed, but there is no blood or dark cola color.
My urine amount feels slightly less than usual over the last few days, but I have no burning or pain when passing urine.
My abdomen feels somewhat bloated and full, but my eyes and skin are not yellow, and I have not had any unusual bleeding or bruises.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, sore throat, or skin infections in the past month.
No, I do not feel unusually sensitive to cold weather, and my bowels and skin have been quite normal.
My appetite is slightly down because of the fullness in my stomach, but I have not had any nausea, vomiting, or chronic diarrhea.
No, I have not had any surgery, long airplane flights, or periods of staying in bed.
I have taken amlodipine for high blood pressure for three years without any change in dose, so this sudden whole-body swelling is completely new.
No, I do not take pain relievers like ibuprofen, steroids, or any hormonal medications.
I have had type 2 diabetes for 15 years; my blood sugar control has not been very good lately, but I take metformin every day.
I have had high blood pressure for about 10 years, which I manage with my daily blood pressure pill.
I have not had any known heart attacks, strokes, or diabetic eye problems, but I have not had my kidneys checked in over a year.
I try to keep my food from being overly salty, and my daily routine is mostly sedentary with very little exercise.
Other than diabetes and high blood pressure, I have no other chronic illnesses and have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I take metformin 500 mg twice daily and amlodipine 5 mg once daily, and I do not take any herbal medicines or nutritional supplements.
No, I do not have any allergies to medications or foods.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I do not drink any alcohol, and I have never had hepatitis or liver disease.
I am a retired homemaker and live quietly at home with my husband.
My mother had diabetes, but no one in my family has had kidney disease, dialysis, or early heart failure.
I feel like my body is somehow holding onto a huge amount of fluid.
I was very worried that my heart might be failing and filling my body with water.
I was hoping you could prescribe water pills to help me drain this excess water out.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg, heart rate 76 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6 °C, and oxygen saturation 98% on ambient air.
Marked bilateral periorbital edema is present; conjunctivae are normal without pallor and sclerae are anicteric.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules.
Jugular venous pulse is not elevated, with no visible jugular venous distension at 45 degrees.
Bilateral lung fields are clear to auscultation with normal vesicular breath sounds and no crackles or wheezing.
Regular rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no third heart sound, fourth heart sound, or audible heart murmurs.
Mild generalized abdominal fullness is noted without dilated abdominal wall veins or caput medusae.
Tympanic to percussion throughout; no shifting dullness or fluid wave detected.
Soft and non-tender to palpation throughout; liver and spleen are not palpable below the costal margins.
No tenderness elicited on percussion over either costovertebral angle.
Marked 3+ pitting edema present symmetrically over both lower extremities extending up to the midthighs, along with mild pitting puffiness in both hands.
Calf circumferences are symmetric bilaterally with no local tenderness, warmth, or palpable venous cords.
Skin over the lower extremities appears tight and pale from fluid retention, with no erythema, petechiae, or ulcerations.
